message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (dir. Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** (dir. Stanley Kubrick) | Atmospheric dread, iconic imagery, and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** (dir. John Carpenter) | A tense, claustrophobic alien invasion with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (dir. Jonathan Demme) | A psychological thriller with unforgettable characters. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (dir. Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered the found‑footage style and created a new wave of horror. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (dir. Danny Boyle) | Fast‑moving, visceral zombie outbreak with a strong emotional core. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (dir. James Wan) | Dark, inventive traps and a twisty narrative that sparked a franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (dir. Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found‑footage that made audiences feel like they were watching real events. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (dir. James Wan) | A modern classic that blends folklore with genuine scares. |
| 2013 | **It Follows** (dir. David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the supernatural with a relentless, creeping threat. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (dir. Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burn, period‑accurate horror that builds dread through atmosphere. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (dir. Jordan Peele) | A sharp social satire wrapped in a chilling thriller. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (dir. John Krasinski) | Tension built around silence, with a strong family dynamic. |
| 2020 | **Midsommar** (dir. Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that turns the genre on its head with unsettling rituals. |
| 2021 | **The Invisible Man** (dir. Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of a classic tale with smart pacing and strong performances. |
| 2022 | **Evil Dead Rise** (dir. Lee Cronin) | A fresh, gritty take on the franchise with intense gore and humor. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (dir. Gerard Johnstone) | A creepy, tech‑savvy horror that taps into our fears of AI. |

Feel free to pick any that match your mood—whether you’re after psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a modern twist on classic tropes. Enjoy the scares!
